provenance: contributor's own paid self-test, not a customer payment
summary: A verifier that resolves the signing key as 'the current key only' (ignoring published key history) is non-conformant per §7.4 and produces a false negative the moment a signer rotates a key. This is a general failure mode, not a quirk of one ledger: any spec that does not pin how historical keys are resolved will rot the first time a signer rotates. The vector pins the requirement: a conformant verifier MUST resolve the signing key by key_id against the full key set (current + history).

history_aware.description: Resolves the signing key by key_id against current + history. Conformant per §7.3/§7.4.

current_key_only.description: Pins the live key only; never consults history. Non-conformant. Rejects a validly-signed historical entry — the false-negative trap.
current_key_only.expected: invalid (false negative on a valid entry)

guards: SPEC §7.4 (historical public keys MUST remain retrievable for >= 90 days past rotation) + §7.3 (verify against signer.public_key implies the verifier must hold the key that signed the envelope). A current-key-only resolver violates both, so it is not a conformant verifier.
